title: Improving pneumonia diagnoses using pulse oximetry at rural health institutions in southern Ethiopia: Protocol for a cluster-randomized controlled trial
author: Solomon Hailemariam
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.88mhzu6
materials: 4 School of Medicine, Dilla University, Dilla, Ethiopia
b Fever: axillary temperature > 37.5 degree Celsius
Reliability of pulse oximetry from pilot study
IMCI: Integrated Management of Childhood Illness
SPSS: Statistical Package for Social Sciences
Ethics approval and consent to participate
Date of registration in primary registry | 14/06/2018

steps.title: Obtain approvals and consent
steps.instruction: Secure ethical approval from Hawassa University IRB (ref IRB/009//2017) and Norway REK (ref 2017/2473/REK sør-øst); obtain written permission from Gedeo Zone Health Department and district offices; obtain informed verbal consent from each caregiver after explaining study purpose, voluntary nature, oximetry procedure, and confidentiality.

steps.title: Select and randomize health centres
steps.instruction: From the 38 health centres in Gedeo Zone, randomly select 24 that treat at least one pneumonia case per day; use SPSS at the University of Bergen to generate the list; allocate 12 centres to the intervention arm (IMCI + pulse oximetry) and 12 to the control arm (IMCI only).

steps.title: Conduct pilot reliability study
steps.instruction: Before randomisation, enrol 60 children aged 2–59 months; train a nurse supervisor who then trains two nurses (rater 1 and rater 2); each measures oxygen saturation twice, 5 minutes apart, with the ADC® Adimals 2150 pulse oximeter; assess agreement with Bland‑Altman (mean differences –0.2 % (95 % CI –3.5 to 3.1) and 0.1 % (95 % CI –4.2 to 4.5)) and intraclass correlation coefficients (supervisor vs rater 1 ICC 0.98 (95 % CI 0.97‑0.99), supervisor vs rater 2 ICC 0.96 (0.94‑0.98), rater 1 ICC 0.91 (0.85‑0.95)).

steps.title: Train health workers
steps.instruction: Provide IMCI training by an IMCI‑trained paediatrician using WHO videos, written documents, and practical exercises; validate classification with video‑based case exercises; for the intervention arm, add a full day of pulse oximetry training including lectures, hands‑on sessions with the ADC® Adimals 2150, and regular supervision by the research team.

steps.title: Enroll eligible children
steps.instruction: From September 2018 to February 2019, enrol children 2–59 months presenting with cough or difficult breathing; exclude children with cough >2 weeks whose differential diagnosis includes tuberculosis; obtain verbal caregiver consent before any study procedure.

steps.title: Perform IMCI clinical assessment
steps.instruction: Collect detailed history and socio‑demographic data; measure weight, length/height, and mid‑upper‑arm circumference; calculate weight‑for‑age, weight‑for‑height, and height‑for‑age Z‑scores using WHO Anthro software; record temperature and respiratory rate by counting breaths for a full minute while the child is quiet; define fast breathing as ≥50 breaths/min for 2‑11 months or ≥40 breaths/min for 12‑59 months; assess general danger signs (unable to drink/breastfeed, vomiting everything, convulsions, lethargic/unconscious) and chest wall indrawing.

steps.title: Measure oxygen saturation (intervention)
steps.instruction: In the intervention arm, use the pediatric fingertip pulse oximeter ADC® Adimals 2150; ensure the child is calm and a stable high‑amplitude plethysmographic waveform is present for 1 minute; record two SpO₂ readings 5 minutes apart; calculate the average and record the percentage.

steps.title: Classify severe pneumonia
steps.instruction: Define severe pneumonia as a child with cough or difficult breathing plus any general danger sign OR fast breathing plus chest indrawing; for the intervention arm, also classify as severe if average SpO₂ < 90 % (cut‑off from WHO guideline). Record the classification for each child.

steps.title: Manage treatment and referral
steps.instruction: Treat all children with pneumonia immediately according to national guidelines; refer urgently to the nearest hospital any child classified with severe pneumonia or with SpO₂ < 90 %; at the day‑14 visit, refer any child whose cough persists.

steps.title: Schedule and conduct follow‑up
steps.instruction: Arrange follow‑up visits on day 2, day 5, and day 14 after enrolment; if a visit is missed, contact the family the next day; if the family cannot be located, phone the participant, relatives, or neighbours to obtain information on death, relocation, or hospitalization; classify children not reachable as lost to follow‑up.

steps.title: Collect and enter study data
steps.instruction: Use a structured paper questionnaire to capture health‑worker characteristics, caregiver socio‑demographics, child clinical data, and cost data; double‑enter all records by two trained data clerks into EpiData version 3.1 (The EpiData Association, Odense, Denmark, 2004); perform range and consistency checks, cleanse data, and resolve inconsistencies against the original questionnaire.

steps.title: Conduct cost‑effectiveness assessment
steps.instruction: Adopt a societal perspective; gather market prices and interview participants for resource use; categorize costs as programme (pulse oximeter purchase, batteries, health‑worker time, training materials) or patient (out‑of‑pocket consultation, transportation, caregiver time valued at unskilled wage rates); estimate direct and indirect costs for severe pneumonia management and compute the incremental cost‑effectiveness ratio per additional severe pneumonia case identified.

steps.title: Perform statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze data with STATA version 15; compare baseline characteristics using independent‑sample t‑tests (continuous) and chi‑square tests (categorical); estimate intervention effects on primary and secondary outcomes with mixed‑effects logistic regression including a random intercept for health‑centre clustering; report odds ratios with 95 % confidence intervals; obtain the intraclass correlation coefficient for outcomes from the random‑effects model.

steps.title: Report results and trial registration
steps.instruction: Present primary outcome (severe pneumonia per IMCI + SpO₂) and secondary outcomes (referral rates, treatment failure on day 14, cost data) using intention‑to‑treat analysis; note that no Data Safety and Monitoring Board is required because IMCI is routine care and no adverse effects are expected; cite trial registration PACTR201807164196402 (registered 14/06/2018) and IRB approvals; disseminate findings to stakeholders.
